newsitem.title: UK: US stocks in London steady, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: US stocks in London steady, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. shares were little changed from Wall Street's closing levels as a scarcity of corporate and economic news kept many European investors away.
Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's upcomging testimony to U.S. lawmakers also kept players on the defensive, dealers said.
Greenspan is to testify before the Senate Banking Committee at 1500 GMT/1000 EST on Wednesday and before a House Banking subcommittee on March 5.
The Fed chief's twice yearly report to Congress on the economy and monetary policy, called for under a law known as Humphrey-Hawkins, is watched closely by financial markets.
The report comes with the unemployment rate at 5.4 percent and underlying inflation hovering near 30-year lows.

Micron Technology was up $1/4 at $37-1/8 after rising $2-5/8 in New York on Monday, lifted by comments from Merrill Lynch analyst Thomas Kurlak who said that the recent pullback in semiconductor stocks was due to portfolio selling.
Kurlak said memory chip stocks such as Micron and Texas Instruments, up $1/8 at $82-1/4 had the most upside potential, a Merrill source said.
Motorola was down $1/4 at $58-3/8 following press reports that the company was losing sales to rivals in the U.S. digital telephone business.

A survey from from Dataquest Inc, scheduled to be released today, show early winners in the digital phone battle to be Sweden's Telefon AB L.M. Ericcson and Finland's Oy Nokia, the Wall Street Journal said.
The March S&P 500 futures contract was up 1.35 at 813.90 by 1105 GMT, while the March T-bond rose 4/32 to 112-24/32. The yield on the cash 30-year long bond was standing at 6.65 percent.
